Prevention: Avoid crop rotation with, or nearby planting of, peppers, eggplants, cotton, maize, sorghum, cowpea or okra because bollworms like these crops.
In case of low bollworm populations in the area, grow one or two maize rows around the tomato field to reduce the pressure of the pest on the tomato.
Collect and dispose of any infested fruit before the insect completes its lifecycle.
Monitoring: Eggs are laid on the upper leaf surface, while the larvae feed inside the fruit.
Adults are yellow-brown with some irregular crosslines on the forewings.
Search for young caterpillars on leaves below highest open flowers and on fruit bases.
When the first few <1 cm long caterpillars are detected, you may consider action.
Search for small, darkened caterpillar entry holes at the base of the tomato near the fruit stem under base leaves of the old flower.
No threshold information is available management of this pest but green control measures can be carried out as soon as the pest is seen.
Yellow measures should only be considered if they are economic.
Direct Control: Handpick caterpillars from flower bud tips and fruit bases and destroy them.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
Apply insecticides during flowering, when eggs hatch so that newly hatched larvae are killed.
Only the young, small (<1 cm long) larvae that are still outside the fruits can be controlled.
Larvae inside fruits are protected from sprays with contact pesticides.
Benzoate 5.7% WG Chanrai- Emaben, Beta-cypermethrine 100g/ l (Atiko), Acetamiprid (Allice 20Sp), Alpha cypermethrine 100g/l.
